lines.trans: I want you to leave.
From the restaurant?
From my life.
And what if I do not want that?
The child needs a father.
He does need one.
But not you.
Vika, I am not going anywhere anyway.
In that case, I will go to Vitya right now.
And demand that he fire you.
If they do not fire you, I will quit myself.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'I', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Well then, Victor, do you surrender?

examples.text: Русские не сдаются, особенно когда играют против олигархов.
examples.trans: Russians do not surrender, especially when playing against oligarchs.
Do not call me an oligarch.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'want', paired with 'захотеть'.

examples.trans: What did you want?
So what did you want?
I want coffee.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'so that, in order to', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Well then, Victor, do you surrender?

examples.text: Сколько тебе надо будет мяса продать, чтобы рассчитаться?
examples.trans: How much meat will you have to sell to settle up with me?
Do you think that I am blind?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'you (informal)', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: А ты так и не научился играть в покер.
examples.trans: And you still have not learned to play poker.
Hi, you braked just in time.
I will raise him as my own.

meanings.en: to leave, to go away, to walk out
meanings.note: Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'left, would leave', paired with 'уходить'.

examples.trans: I want him to leave.
She has already gone home.
So should I leave?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'from/out of', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Are you satisfied? You ruined the surprise.

examples.text: А это что такое? Тоже сюрприз для Феди?
examples.trans: And what is this? Also a surprise for Fedya?

examples.text: Пожалуйста, извините за мой внешний вид.
examples.trans: You are welcome, excuse my appearance.

meanings.note: Borrowed from French 'restaurant' (from 'restaurer', to restore strength with rich broth); entered Russian in the early 19th century.

examples.text: Есть идея провести в ресторане акцию «Месяц Прованса».
examples.trans: There is an idea to hold a 'Month of Provence' promotion in the restaurant.

examples.text: Смысл любой акции в ресторане — это получить прибыль.
examples.trans: The point of any promotion in a restaurant is to make a profit.

examples.text: Да, и ресторан, но начинал я водителем.
examples.trans: Yes, and a restaurant, though I started out as a driver.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'my', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Give him my phone number.

examples.text: Я точно знаю, что это мой ребёнок.
examples.trans: I know for sure that this is my child.
And here are my winnings.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'life' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Risking a human life for the sake of a victory!
From my life.

examples.text: Но всю жизнь ищем близкого человека.
examples.trans: But our whole life we look for a close person.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'and, but', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Well then, Victor, do you surrender?

examples.text: Русские не сдаются, особенно когда играют против олигархов.
examples.trans: Russians do not surrender, especially when playing against oligarchs.
Do not call me an oligarch.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'what, that', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Well then, Victor, do you surrender?

examples.text: Сколько тебе надо будет мяса продать, чтобы рассчитаться?
examples.trans: How much meat will you have to sell to settle up with me?
Do you think that I am blind?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'if', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Но если я приведу человека, который съест твой антрекот.
examples.trans: But if I bring a person who eats your entrecote.

examples.text: А если его съедаешь, то за счёт можно не платить.
examples.trans: And if you eat it up, you do not have to pay the bill.

examples.text: А что, если я этого не хочу?
examples.trans: And what if I do not want that?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'this', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: I am ready to accept this child.

examples.text: А это что такое? Тоже сюрприз для Феди?
examples.trans: And what is this? Also a surprise for Fedya?

examples.text: Почему это лежало в твоём ящике с носками?
examples.trans: Why was this lying in your drawer with your socks?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'not', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Русские не сдаются, особенно когда играют против олигархов.
examples.trans: Russians do not surrender, especially when playing against oligarchs.
Do not call me an oligarch.

examples.text: А как же мне тебя называть?
examples.trans: Then what should I call you?

meanings.note: Formed with a diminutive/expressive Slavic suffix adding warmth or small scale. Common masculine noun meaning 'child / baby' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: I am ready to accept this child.

examples.text: Я точно знаю, что это мой ребёнок.
examples.trans: I know for sure that this is my child.
It is dangerous for the baby.

meanings.note: Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('needed').

examples.trans: You need to be more careful behind the wheel.

examples.text: Тебе нужно прекратить ездить за рулём.
examples.trans: You need to stop driving behind the wheel.

examples.text: Шеф, нужно срочно что-то делать с этим мясом.
examples.trans: Chef, we urgently need to do something with this meat.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'father' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: А что люди скажут, когда узнают про тебя на работе?
examples.trans: And what will people say when they find out about you at work?

examples.text: Марин, у меня нет никаких романов на работе.
examples.trans: Marina, I do not have any romances at work.
Otherwise the owner of the hotel will fire you.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'but', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Русские не сдаются, особенно когда играют против олигархов.
examples.trans: Russians do not surrender, especially when playing against oligarchs.
The meat king of Russia?
Alright then, let us show our cards.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'everything', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Take all this meat for yourself.

examples.text: Люди будут съедать всё наше мясо бесплатно.
examples.trans: People will eat up all our meat for free.
Is everything clear to you?

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: Sounds great, right?
I hope you enjoy it here.

examples.text: Вика, я всё равно никуда не уйду.
examples.trans: Vika, I am not going anywhere anyway.

meanings.en: nowhere, not anywhere (direction/destination, used with не or нет)
meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'nowhere', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Вика, я всё равно никуда не уйду.
examples.trans: Vika, I am not going anywhere anyway.

examples.text: Слушайте, да не нужно вам никуда ехать.
examples.trans: Listen, you don't need to go anywhere.
I wasn't hiding anywhere!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'in, into', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Well then, Victor, do you surrender?

examples.text: Русские не сдаются, особенно когда играют против олигархов.
examples.trans: Russians do not surrender, especially when playing against oligarchs.
Do not call me an oligarch.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronominal determiner meaning 'such', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: А ты так и не научился играть в покер.
examples.trans: And you still have not learned to play poker.

examples.text: В таком случае мне здесь больше нечего делать.
examples.trans: In that case, there is nothing left for me to do here.

examples.text: А это что такое? Тоже сюрприз для Феди?
examples.trans: And what is this? Also a surprise for Fedya?

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'лучай'). Common masculine noun meaning 'case, occasion, incident' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: В таком случае мне здесь больше нечего делать.
examples.trans: In that case, there is nothing left for me to do here.

examples.text: Жаль только, что наш усатый генератор случайных идей не знает.
examples.trans: Too bad our moustached generator of random ideas does not know.
A common case, overeating is to blame for everything.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'ейчас').

examples.trans: Calm down right now!
We will make it right now, Victoria Sergeyevna.
Money is tight right now, take the meat.

meanings.note: Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'will go', paired with 'идти'.

examples.text: В таком случае я сейчас пойду к Вите.
examples.trans: In that case, I will go to Vitya right now.
May I go?
Let's go home.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'to, towards', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Well then, Victor, do you surrender?

examples.text: Русские не сдаются, особенно когда играют против олигархов.
examples.trans: Russians do not surrender, especially when playing against oligarchs.

examples.text: А как же мне тебя называть?
examples.trans: Then what should I call you?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'and', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Well then, Victor, do you surrender?

examples.text: Русские не сдаются, особенно когда играют против олигархов.
examples.trans: Russians do not surrender, especially when playing against oligarchs.
Do not call me an oligarch.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'требовать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'will demand'.

examples.text: Надо всё сделать и потребовать вовремя.
examples.trans: We need to do everything and will demand on time.

examples.text: На нашей кухне все умеют потребовать.
examples.trans: In our kitchen everyone knows how to will demand.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'he', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Give him my phone number.
Why did she call late yesterday?

examples.text: У Феди скоро день рождения, она звонила посоветоваться.
examples.trans: Fedya's birthday is coming up soon, she called to ask for advice.

meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'волить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to fire, to dismiss', paired with 'увольнять'.

examples.trans: Otherwise the owner of the hotel will fire you.

examples.text: Сенечка, зайчик, я уволилась, как ты сказал.
examples.trans: Senechka, little bunny, I quit just as you said.

examples.text: И потребую, чтобы он тебя уволил.
examples.trans: And demand that he fire you.

meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'волиться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'will quit / resign'.

examples.text: Ты можешь уволиться в любой момент.
examples.trans: You can quit at any moment.
She quit herself.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'myself', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: He started kissing me himself!
Senechka, he started it himself!
What do you think yourself?

meanings.note: Prefix 'под-' ('under, up to') indicates approaching or supporting from below (stem 'ождать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'wait', paired with 'ждать'.

examples.trans: Wait, I'll be right there.
Wait a minute.

examples.text: Подожди, Нин, ты не поняла. Это же стыдно!
examples.trans: Wait, Nina, you don't get it. It's shameful!

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'do', paired with 'сделать'.

examples.text: В таком случае мне здесь больше нечего делать.
examples.trans: In that case, there is nothing left for me to do here.

examples.text: Сделайте мне кто-нибудь бутерброд с тунцом.
examples.trans: Someone make me a tuna sandwich.
We will make it right now, Victoria Sergeyevna.

meanings.note: Abstract feminine noun formed with the Slavic suffix '-ость' ('-ness, -ity') from the corresponding adjective. Common feminine noun meaning 'nonsense, foolishness' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Vika, wait, do not do anything foolish.
What nonsense?
Don't talk nonsense.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian cardinal or ordinal numeral meaning 'one', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Introduce it, introduce it.
No, this is just my driver.

examples.text: Да Вика шутит, слушай, какой водитель?
examples.trans: Vika is joking, listen, what driver?

meanings.note: Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'will leave', paired with 'оставлять'.

examples.trans: I won't leave him on his own.
Leave me alone!

examples.text: Вика, ну он одинокий. Я же не оставлю его одного.
examples.trans: Vika, come on, he's all alone. I can't just leave him on his own.
